description: The Safe Hospitals initiative of the Pan American Health Organization defines a safe hospital as a health facility whose services remain accessible and functioning at maximum capacity, within the same infrastructure, immediately after a natural disaster, with access routes, water, power and telecommunications still available. Its main tool, the Hospital Safety Index, was developed by PAHO's Disaster Mitigation Advisory Group with Latin American and Caribbean experts to estimate the probability that a hospital or health facility will keep functioning in emergencies, based on structural, non-structural and functional factors, the environment and the health services network. An evaluation team scores 145 areas of the hospital on the standardised Safe Hospitals Checklist and enters the validated scores into a calculator that weights each item by its importance; a second-edition Guide for Evaluators explains the method. Coverage: health facilities anywhere; widely used in the Americas. Access: guides and forms from PAHO and its IRIS repository. Licence: PAHO publication terms, not read on the day; free. Caveats: PAHO states that the index does not replace detailed vulnerability studies. Simulation uses are rapid, comparable safety scores for hospitals as inputs to health system resilience and prioritisation models. Related records: the healthsites.io and hospital location records for facility inventories.
